To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hybrid catalysts prepared by anchoring the [Rh(codd)Cl]  complex on mesoporous molecular sieve supports exhibit comparable or even higher polymerization activity than the homogeneous catalyst.

The hybrid catalysts prepared by anchoring the [Rh(codd)Cl] 1.5 complex on siliceou mesoporous molecular sieve differing in pore size and architecture exhibited higher activity than the homogeneous catalyst in the polymerization reactions of phenylacetylne and 4-ethyl-N-(4- [(trimethylsily)ethynyl)benzylidenc}aniline.

hybrid catalysts based on [Rh(cod)(Cl)2] anchored on MCM-48, MCM-41 and SBA- 15 mesoporous molecular sieve are efficient in polymerization of phenyacetylene and acetylenes bearing aromatic substituents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
preparation of hybrid catalysts based on mesoporous molecular sieve supports and [Rh(cod)(Cl) 2 ] 2 complex.
the synthesis of new hybrid catalysts for acetylene polymerization and the influence of the support structure on their catalytic activity.
the synthesis, characterization, and catalytic properties of hybrid catalysts based on siliceous ordered mesoporous molecular sieve supports (MCM-48 and MCM-41) and the SBA-15 material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all three catalysts are active in the polymerization reaction, but the activity is strongly influenced by the structure and the pore size of the support material.
the catalytic activity and the polymer properties of the prepared hybrid catalysts are determined by the structure and the accessibility of the mesoporous surface.
the mesostructured catalysts are not superior to the homogeneous [Rh(cod)(Cl)] 2 catalyst in the polymerization reactions studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hybrid catalysts prepared by anchoring [Rh(codon)Cl] 3 on MCM-48, SBA-15 and MCM-41 mesoporous molecular sieve are promising candidates for acetylenes polymerization, especially in the case of the polymerization of 4-ethinyl-N-(4-(trimethylsily)ethinyl)benzylidened)aniline.
the mesoporous structure and the accessibility of the mesopore surface play a key role in determining the activity of the hybrid catalysts for acetylenes polymerization. 2009 Elsevier Ltd.
the catalytic activity and the polymer molecular weight are affected mainly by the accessibility of the mesoporous surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mesoporous molecular sieve supports with high surface area and large pore volume, such as SBA-15, are very promising for preparation of hybrid catalysts for acetylenes polymerization.

the catalytic activity of supported catalysts in acetylene polymerization can be tuned by changing the pore size and pore architecture of mesoporous supports, while the microstructure of the polymers is independent of the catalyst support.

the catalytic performance of supported rhodium complexes in the acetylene polymerization is not limited by diffusion of monomers and growing polymer chains through the pores of catalysts, as is usually observed for other polymerization reactions.
